title: Truthfulness and its company
hookLine: a man with no excuse tells the truth anyway, and a verse comes down about the company he keeps

cards: Ka'b ibn Malik had no excuse. The army had marched out to Tabuk, and he had simply stayed home, putting it off day after day until it was too late.
When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came back, others lined up with reasons, and he accepted their word. Then it was Ka'b's turn. He could talk well.
He knew he could win the moment. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, he told the Prophet instead: I had no excuse.

teach.b: It cost him. Ka'b, with two others who also told the truth, was set apart. People stopped speaking to them.
Ka'b says the earth, wide as it was, felt narrow. Then the Qur'an spoke about the three. Surah al-Tawbah describes them, and their repentance accepted, then turns to everyone listening.
In Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! Be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful." Not only be truthful. Be with the truthful.
Sidq is a virtue, and it is also a company.
And Ka'b, after all of it, said, in paraphrase from Bukhari: Allah saved me only through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is to speak nothing but the truth for the rest of my life.

Then the Prophet's own description, from Ibn Mas'ud, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to the Garden, and a person keeps telling the truth until he becomes a siddiq, one utterly truthful.
Each true sentence is a step, and the steps add up to a name.
That's why the company matters. A circle where everyone shades the story makes the next lie cheaper. A circle of truthful friends makes a sentence like Ka'b's easier to say.

how: Islamic teaching draws on Qur'an 9:119 and the story of Ka'b ibn Malik: truthfulness is both a personal virtue and a matter of keeping truthful company.

o: truthfulness, even when an excuse would be easier
telling people kindly only what they hope to hear
keeping a promise to repay a debt right on time

s: Ka'b gave the Prophet a clever excuse
he said he had no excuse, though he knew he could have argued well.
the verse says 'be with the truthful,' not only 'be truthful'
Pickthall: be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful.
truthfulness costs nothing in Ka'b's story
he was set apart, and said the wide earth felt narrow.

games.q: you're Ka'b. you stayed home from Tabuk with no good reason. others are offering excuses and being believed. it's your turn. what do you say?
o: give a good excuse; you speak well.
say plainly: I had no excuse.
ask to come back another day.
games.why: he told the truth, was set apart for a time, and al-Tawbah later told of the three whose repentance was accepted.

practice: Bring to mind the people you spend the most time with, in person or on a screen, and ask of each, without judging anyone: with this person, is it easier to tell the truth, or harder?
Then hold the face of one person who tells you the truth even when it's awkward. If you pray, you can ask to be among the truthful.

wordCard.voice: Sidq. Truthfulness: in the tongue, in the heart, and in the company you keep, step by step toward becoming a siddiq. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: truthfulness; a siddiq is one utterly truthful.

carryVoice: Your line: with the truthful. A virtue, and a company to keep. I'll be here tomorrow.

sources.q: O ye who believe! Be careful of your duty to Allah, and be with the truthful.

sources.ref: Qur'an 9:118 (the three who were left behind; the earth, vast as it was, straitened for them)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4418 (Ka'b ibn Malik: staying behind from Tabuk, no excuse, saved by truthfulness)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6094 (Ibn Mas'ud: truthfulness leads to righteousness; written as a siddiq)
